venue.name: West Coast NEST
venue.description: West Coast NEST (Nature. Education. Sustainability. Transformation.) is a learning network convened through the Clayoquot Biosphere Trust, covering the west coast of Vancouver Island from Hesquiaht in the north to Ucluelet in the south. It is not a place you visit. Its office is at 316 Main St in Tofino, and most of the courses listed on its site are run by other regional organizations, each of which you book with directly. What NEST delivers itself is a paid planning service that builds a custom learning trip for a group, plus its own events such as Biodiversity Discovery Days and the Coastal Pathways youth camp.
venue.seasonal_notes: Biodiversity Discovery Days ran May 21 to 24, 2026 across Ucluelet, Tofino and Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, a multi day run of guided walks, cultural experiences, workshops and restoration activities with a region wide species count. Most of those events were free, with a few ticketed. Coastal Pathways, a four day youth camp over spring break, is listed for March 22 to 25, 2027.

programs.name: Customized Programs: West Coast NEST
programs.description: West Coast NEST's Education Coordinator works with a group to build a learning trip in the Clayoquot Biosphere Reserve region. The service covers the itinerary, coordinating the educational programs and learning spaces, suggestions for travel and accommodation, a welcome and community orientation on arrival, and one point of contact before and during the stay. The programs themselves are run by regional partners on topics such as Indigenous culture, nature, sustainability, science, language, history, outdoor education and art, and each one booked costs extra on top of the planning charge. To start, you email the Director of Education for a booking form.
programs.our_note: This is a planning service rather than an outing. You pay West Coast NEST for the hours it spends building your itinerary, then pay each partner separately for the tours and workshops themselves. It earns its keep if you want several stops around Tofino and Ucluelet in one trip and would rather not chase a dozen organisations yourself.
programs.practical_summary: The planning charge and the email to start are published, and the office is on Main Street in Tofino. Ages, group size, how much notice is needed, washrooms and somewhere to eat are all unstated, because the visit itself happens at partner sites. Worth settling all of that on the first call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Planning is $150 for the first hour and $50 an hour after that. Every educational tour or workshop booked through a regional partner is paid for on top.
programs.evidence: Customized planning is $150 for the first hour, then $50/hour.

programs.name: Coastal Pathways: Skills, Stories & Futures
programs.description: A four day camp over spring break, March 22 to 25, 2027, run by West Coast NEST. Mornings are for grades 6 to 8 and afternoons for grades 9 to 12. The camp is built around building confidence and leadership and introducing young people to coastal career paths in science, sustainability, tourism and the arts. Families arrange their own travel and beds, with preferred rates offered at Pacific Sands Beach Resort and Tofino Resort and Marina. Only an interest list is open so far and no fee is published.
programs.what_children_do: Four half days of hands on activities, guided field experiences and workshops, led by West Coast NEST staff alongside local professionals, environmental organizations, artists and Nuu chah nulth knowledge holders. Mornings are the grades 6 to 8 group, afternoons grades 9 to 12.
programs.our_note: This one is for older students, not preschoolers, and it runs during spring break rather than in school time. The fee, the daily start and finish times and the meeting place are all still to come, so put your name on the interest list if you want the details when they land.
programs.practical_summary: The dates and the grade split are set and the camp runs on the west coast over spring break 2027. The fee, the daily times, where to meet and what to bring are not published yet, and families sort out their own travel and accommodation.

gaps: West Coast NEST is a network, not a place to visit. Almost every course on its site is run by another organization and is booked with that organization directly, so only the two offerings NEST delivers itself are recorded here.
no youngest age is published anywhere, and nothing on the site says whether preschool or daycare groups are served

the customized planning service publishes no age or grade range, no group size limit and no minimum notice; it is filed under both the K to 7 and the 8 to 12 outdoor school headings on the site, but that is a browsing category rather than a stated range, so no range is recorded
no fee is published for the Coastal Pathways spring break camp, and no daily start or finish times, meeting place or kit list
washrooms, somewhere to eat, rain shelter, step free access and bus parking are not addressed, because the activities happen at partner sites rather than at the office
the customized planning charge carries no year or season, so it is not clear how current it is
photographs on the site mostly carry no alt text at all, and the homepage banner's alt is a label rather than a description of the picture; both recorded images use the site's own alt text
the About page says over 40 partner organizations while the customized programs page says over 30, so the count is approximate either way

Biodiversity Discovery Days is a community event with most sessions free and open to all ages, but it is not a bookable group offering and the 2026 dates have passed, so it is noted against the venue rather than recorded as a program
